To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the filamentation of two ASNS proteins is regulated by glucose availability, and the Asn1 protein forms filaments in an Asn2-dependent manner.
the two ASNS proteins are capable of forming distinct cytoophidias in diauxic phase and that glucose deprivation induces cytoophidia formation of ASNS.

asparagine synthase (ASN1) and CTP (cytidine triphosphate) synthase (CTP1) are two metabolic enzyme cytoophidia that form adjacent to each other in Saccharomyes cerevisiae, and that ASN1 cytoophidium formation is regulated by a key residue, Asp330, which resides at the dimer interface of ASN1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
cytoophidia formation and its biological functions.
the filamentation of two important metabolic enzymes in S. cerevisiae.
the filamentation of asparaginyl-tRNA synthetase and the relationship with CTP synthase.

the ASNS filament formation is dependent on Asn2 but not on Asn1, and that Asn1 and Ctp1 cytoophidias are closely associated in the cell.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the filamentation of both ASNS and its paralog, CTPS, are regulated by glucose and glutamine levels in the cell.
Asn1 cytoplasmic filaments are essential for Asn2 filament formation.
the filamentation of both ASNS and the paralogous CTPS are induced by nutrient deprivation and are essential for cell survival.

the filamentation of metabolic enzymes is not a unique feature of CTPS, but also occurs in ASNS.
